commit 9d7fd7cd84fd35d96f0720292980ab708fd7b116
Author: ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Oct 11 16:16:40 2026 +0300

    fix(browser-ext): package a comment-stripped manifest — CWS strict-JSON upload rejection
    
    The CWS uploader parses manifest.json STRICTLY and rejected the fa1.dev
    zip: 'manifest.json:17:2: missing value' (owner report 2026-10-11) —
    the source manifest carries // comments that Chrome's local loader
    tolerates. The whole toolchain normalized comments for VALIDATION but
    shipped the verbatim file, so every gate was green on a store-invalid
    artifact.
    
    - build_browser_ext.sh: the zip carries a comment-stripped manifest
      (build/pack/manifest.json staged copy; source keeps its comments);
      both the zip-CLI and python-fallback packaging paths.
    - build_browser_ext.sh: strip the staged panel app's PWA manifest
      UNCONDITIONALLY before packaging — a stale gitignored panel/app from
      an earlier --with-app run otherwise fails the single-manifest guard
      on plain local builds (caught by the guard during this fix).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1615
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1615
- **Title**: fix(browser_ext): make manifest.json strict JSON
- **Author**: YuryBY
- **Branch**: `fix/browser-ext-manifest-json` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +39
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T16:47:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T16:47:57Z

## PR Description

## What was broken
`browser_ext/manifest.json` contained 19 `//` comment lines (issue #137 permission rationale, issue #470 embed_relay note). That is not valid JSON, and Chrome refuses to load a manifest with comments (`json.load` fails with `JSONDecodeError` at line 17).

## Fix
- Removed the comment lines from the manifest; `permissions` and all other keys are unchanged (39 permissions before and after).
- Moved the rationale to `browser_ext/README.md` (new "Manifest notes" section).
- Added `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart`: strict `jsonDecode` of the manifest, no comment stripping.

## Verified
- `python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('browser_ext/manifest.json'))"` passes (failed before).
- `dart test test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` passes.
- Not loaded into Chrome.

## PR Description

## What was broken
`browser_ext/manifest.json` contained 19 `//` comment lines (issue #137 permission rationale, issue #470 embed_relay note). That is not valid JSON, and Chrome refuses to load a manifest with comments (`json.load` fails with `JSONDecodeError` at line 17).

## Fix
- Removed the comment lines from the manifest; `permissions` and all other keys are unchanged (39 permissions before and after).
- Moved the rationale to `browser_ext/README.md` (new "Manifest notes" section).
- Added `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart`: strict `jsonDecode` of the manifest, no comment stripping.

## Verified
- `python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('browser_ext/manifest.json'))"` passes (failed before).
- `dart test test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` passes.
- Not loaded into Chrome.

commit 9d7fd7cd84fd35d96f0720292980ab708fd7b116
Author: ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Oct 11 16:16:40 2026 +0300

    fix(browser-ext): package a comment-stripped manifest — CWS strict-JSON upload rejection
    
    The CWS uploader parses manifest.json STRICTLY and rejected the fa1.dev
    zip: 'manifest.json:17:2: missing value' (owner report 2026-10-11) —
    the source manifest carries // comments that Chrome's local loader
    tolerates. The whole toolchain normalized comments for VALIDATION but
    shipped the verbatim file, so every gate was green on a store-invalid
    artifact.
    
    - build_browser_ext.sh: the zip carries a comment-stripped manifest
      (build/pack/manifest.json staged copy; source keeps its comments);
      both the zip-CLI and python-fallback packaging paths.
    - build_browser_ext.sh: strip the staged panel app's PWA manifest
      UNCONDITIONALLY before packaging — a stale gitignored panel/app from

## PR Description

## What was broken
`browser_ext/manifest.json` contained 19 `//` comment lines (issue #137 permission rationale, issue #470 embed_relay note). That is not valid JSON, and Chrome refuses to load a manifest with comments (`json.load` fails with `JSONDecodeError` at line 17).

## Fix
- Removed the comment lines from the manifest; `permissions` and all other keys are unchanged (39 permissions before and after).
- Moved the rationale to `browser_ext/README.md` (new "Manifest notes" section).
- Added `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart`: strict `jsonDecode` of the manifest, no comment stripping.

## Verified
- `python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('browser_ext/manifest.json'))"` passes (failed before).
- `dart test test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` passes.
- Not loaded into Chrome.

      UNCONDITIONALLY before packaging — a stale gitignored panel/app from
      an earlier --with-app run otherwise fails the single-manifest guard
      on plain local builds (caught by the guard during this fix).

    "summary": "fix(browser_ext): make manifest.json strict JSON",
    "description": "## What was broken
`browser_ext/manifest.json` contained 19 `//` comment lines (issue #137 permission rationale, issue #470 embed_relay note). That is not valid JSON, and Chrome refuses to load a manifest with comments (`json.load` fails with `JSONDecodeError` at line 17).

## Fix
- Removed the comment lines from the manifest; `permissions` and all other keys are unchanged (39 permissions before and after).
- Moved the rationale to `browser_ext/README.md` (new "Manifest notes" section).
- Added `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart`: strict `jsonDecode` of the manifest, no comment stripping.

## Verified
- `python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('browser_ext/manifest.json'))"` passes (failed before).
- `dart test test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` passes.
- Not loaded into Chrome."
  }

{
  "key": "pr-1615",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(browser_ext): make manifest.json strict JSON",
    "description": "## What was broken
`browser_ext/manifest.json` contained 19 `//` comment lines (issue #137 permission rationale, issue #470 embed_relay note). That is not valid JSON, and Chrome refuses to load a manifest with comments (`json.load` fails with `JSONDecodeError` at line 17).

## Fix
- Removed the comment lines from the manifest; `permissions` and all other keys are unchanged (39 permissions before and after).
- Moved the rationale to `browser_ext/README.md` (new "Manifest notes" section).
- Added `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart`: strict `jsonDecode` of the manifest, no comment stripping.

## Verified
- `python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('browser_ext/manifest.json'))"` passes (failed before).
- `dart test test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` passes.
- Not loaded into Chrome."
  }
}

      an earlier --with-app run otherwise fails the single-manifest guard
      on plain local builds (caught by the guard during this fix).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                icons: "set[str]" = set()
                top = manifest.get("icons")
                if isinstance(top, dict):
                    icons.update(str(v) for v in top.values() if isinstance(v, str))
                action = manifest.get("action")
                if isinstance(action, dict):
                    di = action.get("default_icon")
                    if isinstance(di, str):
                        icons.add(di)
                    elif isinstance(di, dict):
                        icons.update(str(v) for v in di.values() if isinstance(v, str))
                missing = sorted(i for i in icons if i not in names)
                if missing:
                    error(
                        "manifest-icons",
                        f"{zip_path}: icons referenced by the root manifest "
                        f"missing from the zip: {', '.join(missing)}",
                    )
                    failures += 1

    if failures:
        error(
            "ext-package-check",
            f"{zip_path}: {failures} packaging-shape failure(s) — fix the "
            "build, do not upload this zip (Chrome Web Store would reject "
            "it)",
        )
        return 1

    print(
        f"check: {zip_path} OK — single root manifest.json (MV3), "
        f"{len(names)} entries, icons present, no junk"
    )
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if len(args) != 2 or args[0] not in ("strip", "check"):
        print(
            "usage: ext_package_guard.py strip <staged-app-dir> | "
            "check <zip>",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    return cmd_strip(args[1]) if args[0] == "strip" else cmd_check(args[1])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",

            failures += 1

                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )

17:  // Issue #137 — maximum viable permission set: the generic chrome.*
18:  // bridge (browser_api) exposes every declared namespace to the agent,
19:  // so permissions without access are pure waste. Tier 3 exclusions
20:  // (documented here + permission_matrix.dart):
21:  //   enterprise.*            — device-admin, managed contexts only
22:  //   platformKeys            — ChromeOS-only
23:  //   fileSystemProvider      — ChromeOS-only
24:  //   wallpaper               — ChromeOS-only
25:  //   gcm / instanceID        — legacy push transport, no agent surface
26:  //   devtools                — opens interactive windows, not automation
27:  //   passwords               — chrome exposes no such API at all
28:  // `commands`/`omnibox` are manifest KEYS (below), not permissions.
29:  // `management` is declared but bridge-default-DENIED (self-preservation:
30:  // an injected page must not disable the agent's own extension).
110:      // Issue #470: the embedded fa pane (fa1.dev inside the Outlook tab)
111:      // bridges its provider HTTP to the SW through this relay — page JS has
112:      // no chrome.* and CORS-blocked fetches. all_frames: the pane is a
113:      // cross-origin iframe; top-frame-only injection never sees it. Inert
114:      // everywhere else (it only answers __faEmbed-pane messages).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(

fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart
