The README says: "`manifest.json` is plain JSON (Chrome rejects `//` comments; a guard test parses it strictly)". Hmm — one nuance: Chrome's LOCAL loader (unpacked) has historically been tolerant of comments in some versions... but per the CWS report and repo's own guard (ext_package_guard.py comment: "the Chrome Web Store uploader rejects // comments... even though Chrome's local loader tolerates them"), the repo's own docs say Chrome's local loader tolerates them. The PR's README/PR description claims "Chrome rejects `//` comments". Is that a factual error per the repo's own findings? The ext_package_guard.py says "even though Chrome's local loader tolerates them". And v21_manifest_test.mjs header says "(Chrome's parser is lenient, jsonDecode is not)".

So the PR's README statement "Chrome rejects `//` comments" CONTRADICTS the repo's established understanding ("Chrome's local loader tolerates them; the CWS UPLOADER rejects them"). It's a minor documentation inaccuracy — the true blocker was CWS upload, not local loading. This is a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level docs nit. The rationale direction is still valid (strict JSON is what the store requires; keeping the source in the same shape the store will consume is defensible and simplifies tooling). Not blocking.

### 3. `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` (+17, new)

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:test/test.dart';

void main() {
  test(
    'browser_ext/manifest.json is strict JSON (Chrome rejects comments)',
    () {
      final manifest =
          jsonDecode(File('browser_ext/manifest.json').readAsStringSync())
              as Map<String, dynamic>;
      expect(manifest['manifest_version'], 3);
      expect(manifest['permissions'], isA<List>());
    },
  );
}
```

Issues with the test:

**(a) CWD-dependence / path robustness.** `File('browser_ext/manifest.json')` is a relative path. Dart's `dart test` runs with CWD = package root by default, so it works when run from the repo root. BUT: `dart test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` — still package root CWD. OK. However `package_shape_guard_test.dart` has a `_repoRoot()` helper that resolves the repo root robustly, with a comment: "The repo root (dart test runs with the package root as CWD)". The new test uses a bare relative path. This works under `dart test` from repo root but is fragile if the file is ever run via `dart test` from another directory... Actually, `dart test` always sets CWD to the package root regardless of invocation dir? No — `dart test` must be run from the package directory (it resolves the package config). If you run `dart test` in a subdirectory... package:test resolves paths relative to package root. Actually the CWD of the test isolate is the package root. So `File('browser_ext/manifest.json')` resolves against the package root. That's how `chrome_driver.dart`'s `_repoRoot()` works too — it walks up from Directory.current. package_shape_guard_test uses `_repoRoot()` for `Process.runSync` workingDirectory, being defensive.

Hmm, wait — there's a REAL catch: is this repo's `test/` directory part of the ROOT package (`flutter_agent_harness`) or... the root pubspec is at repo root, test/browser_ext is under the root package's test dir. When you run `dart test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` from repo root, the isolate CWD is repo root. So `browser_ext/manifest.json` resolves fine.

But one edge: `dart test` supports running with `--tags`/presets; the CI runs from repo root. Fine. Still, the more robust pattern in this repo (package_shape_guard_test._repoRoot) exists; the new test's relative path is acceptable since dart test pins CWD. I'd call this a SUGGESTION at most.

**(b) Missing `@TestOn('vm')` annotation.** `dart:io` import means it's VM-only. Other test files in this dir declare `@TestOn('vm')`. Without it, `dart test` default platform is vm anyway. If someone runs the whole suite on the web platform it would fail to compile — but this repo's dart_test.yaml doesn't configure web platforms for the root package. package_shape_guard_test.dart declares `@TestOn('vm')`; the new test doesn't. Minor convention nit (SUGGESTION).

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )

### 1. `browser_ext/manifest.json` (−19 lines)

- `management` declared but bridge-default-DENIED ✓
- embed_relay #470 rationale ✓

The README says: "`manifest.json` is plain JSON (Chrome rejects `//` comments; a guard test parses it strictly)". Hmm — one nuance: Chrome's LOCAL loader (unpacked) has historically been tolerant of comments in some versions... but per the CWS report and repo's own guard (ext_package_guard.py comment: "the Chrome Web Store uploader rejects // comments... even though Chrome's local loader tolerates them"), the repo's own docs say Chrome's local loader tolerates them. The PR's README/PR description claims "Chrome rejects `//` comments". Is that a factual error per the repo's own findings? The ext_package_guard.py says "even though Chrome's local loader tolerates them". And v21_manifest_test.mjs header says "(Chrome's parser is lenient, jsonDecode is not)".

So the PR's README statement "Chrome rejects `//` comments" CONTRADICTS the repo's established understanding ("Chrome's local loader tolerates them; the CWS UPLOADER rejects them"). It's a minor documentation inaccuracy — the true blocker was CWS upload, not local loading. This is a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level docs nit. The rationale direction is still valid (strict JSON is what the store requires; keeping the source in the same shape the store will consume is defensible and simplifies tooling). Not blocking.

### 3. `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` (+17, new)

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:test/test.dart';

void main() {
  test(
    'browser_ext/manifest.json is strict JSON (Chrome rejects comments)',
    () {
      final manifest =
          jsonDecode(File('browser_ext/manifest.json').readAsStringSync())
              as Map<String, dynamic>;
      expect(manifest['manifest_version'], 3);
      expect(manifest['permissions'], isA<List>());
    },
  );
}
```

Issues with the test:

**(a) CWD-dependence / path robustness.** `File('browser_ext/manifest.json')` is a relative path. Dart's `dart test` runs with CWD = package root by default, so it works when run from the repo root. BUT: `dart test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` — still package root CWD. OK. However `package_shape_guard_test.dart` has a `_repoRoot()` helper that resolves the repo root robustly, with a comment: "The repo root (dart test runs with the package root as CWD)". The new test uses a bare relative path. This works under `dart test` from repo root but is fragile if the file is ever run via `dart test` from another directory... Actually, `dart test` always sets CWD to the package root regardless of invocation dir? No — `dart test` must be run from the package directory (it resolves the package config). If you run `dart test` in a subdirectory... package:test resolves paths relative to package root. Actually the CWD of the test isolate is the package root. So `File('browser_ext/manifest.json')` resolves against the package root. That's how `chrome_driver.dart`'s `_repoRoot()` works too — it walks up from Directory.current. package_shape_guard_test uses `_repoRoot()` for `Process.runSync` workingDirectory, being defensive.

Hmm, wait — there's a REAL catch: is this repo's `test/` directory part of the ROOT package (`flutter_agent_harness`) or... the root pubspec is at repo root, test/browser_ext is under the root package's test dir. When you run `dart test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` from repo root, the isolate CWD is repo root. So `browser_ext/manifest.json` resolves fine.

But one edge: `dart test` supports running with `--tags`/presets; the CI runs from repo root. Fine. Still, the more robust pattern in this repo (package_shape_guard_test._repoRoot) exists; the new test's relative path is acceptable since dart test pins CWD. I'd call this a SUGGESTION at most.

**(b) Missing `@TestOn('vm')` annotation.** `dart:io` import means it's VM-only. Other test files in this dir declare `@TestOn('vm')`. Without it, `dart test` default platform is vm anyway. If someone runs the whole suite on the web platform it would fail to compile — but this repo's dart_test.yaml doesn't configure web platforms for the root package. package_shape_guard_test.dart declares `@TestOn('vm')`; the new test doesn't. Minor convention nit (SUGGESTION).

**(c) Tag conventions.** The header comment of package_shape_guard_test says: "no Chrome, no flutter build, so it runs in the default test gate (unlike the rest of test/browser_ext/, which is integration+browser-ext tagged)". The new test needs no Chrome → correctly untagged, runs in the default gate. That's consistent — good. Let me double check the CI "shard_files.py bin-packs manifest-missing new test dirs at runtime" (AGENTS.md:1797) — new test files are picked up at runtime by shard selection, fine.

**(d) Weak assertions.** The test asserts `manifest_version == 3` and `permissions is List`. It does NOT assert:
- The file has no `//` comments... well, jsonDecode strict parse inherently rejects comments — the test's premise is that a strict parse fails if comments are reintroduced. True: jsonDecode fails on `//` lines. So the core protection is real.
- permissions count/content: redundant with v21_manifest_test.mjs (which pins exact sets). OK.

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extension packaging hygiene guard (issue #291).

Chrome Web Store hard-rejects any package with more than one manifest
("More than one manifest found in package: manifest.json,
panel/app/manifest.json") — the exact failure that killed the 2026-09-13
fa-extension.zip upload: the Flutter web build staged under
browser_ext/panel/app ships its own PWA manifest. This script encodes the
store's structural rules as build-time assertions so that whole failure
class dies in CI (and locally), never again at upload.

Two verbs, both wired from scripts/build_browser_ext.sh:

  strip <dir>   Remove the PWA manifest from a STAGED app dir (the
                gitignored browser_ext/panel/app copy — sources in
                flutter_app/web stay untouched): deletes manifest.json and
                drops the <link rel="manifest"> tag from index.html.
                Idempotent (a Flutter template without the tag is a no-op,
                #291 E3). DELETION, not a rename to .webmanifest: inside
                an extension page the PWA manifest is functionally dead
                (extension pages are not installable PWAs, and the CSP
                blocks nothing the manifest needs) — a rename would pass
                the store while shipping dead weight and keeping a link
                nothing consumes.

  check <zip>   Assert the packaged zip's CWS shape and fail loudly:
                  - exactly one manifest.json, at the archive root
                  - no duplicate entry names
                  - no .DS_Store / __MACOSX junk entries
                  - no empty directory entries
                  - the root manifest parses and is manifest_version 3
                  - every icon the root manifest references exists in zip

Errors print as GitHub Actions annotations (::error ...) — rendered by
CI, plain readable text locally — and exit non-zero, failing the build.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import sys

# E2 escape hatch: a future LEGIT nested manifest (e.g. a packaged
# sub-extension) must be allowlisted HERE, in reviewable source, never
# silently. Any manifest.json not at the root and not in this list fails
# the build on purpose.
ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS: "list[str]" = []


def error(rule: str, detail: str) -> None:
    """One ::error workflow-command line; single-line by contract."""
    print(f"::error title={rule}::{detail}", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_strip(staged_dir: str) -> int:
    index_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "index.html")
    if not os.path.isfile(index_path):
        error(
            "ext-package-strip",
            f"strip: {staged_dir}/index.html not found — the staged app "
            "dir is malformed (the Flutter web build always emits one)",
        )
        return 1

    # 1) Delete the nested PWA manifest (missing already → fine, E3).
    manifest_path = os.path.join(staged_dir, "manifest.json")
    removed_manifest = False
    if os.path.isfile(manifest_path):
        os.remove(manifest_path)
        removed_manifest = True

    # 2) Drop the <link rel="manifest"> tag — any attribute order, single
    #    or double quotes. Zero matches → no-op (E3: a Flutter template
    #    change that drops the tag must not fail the build).
    html = open(index_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    html2, n = re.subn(r'<link\b[^>]*\brel=["\']manifest["\'][^>]*>\s*', "", html)
    if n:
        open(index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(html2)

    what = []
    if removed_manifest:
        what.append("manifest.json deleted")
    if n:
        what.append(f"{n} <link rel=manifest> tag(s) dropped")
    print(
        "strip: " + ("; ".join(what) if what else "nothing to strip (clean)")
        + f" [{staged_dir}]"
    )
    return 0


def cmd_check(zip_path: str) -> int:
    import zipfile

    if not os.path.isfile(zip_path):
        error("ext-package-check", f"check: zip not found: {zip_path}")
        return 1

    failures = 0
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as z:
        names = z.namelist()

        # --- single root manifest (THE CWS rule, #291) ------------------
        manifests = sorted(n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == "manifest.json")
        allowed = {"manifest.json", *ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS}
        offenders = [m for m in manifests if m not in allowed]
        if "manifest.json" not in names or offenders:
            error(
                "single-manifest (CWS)",
                f"{zip_path}: {len(manifests)} manifest.json entries — the "
                "Chrome Web Store rejects any package with more than one "
                f"manifest (and it must be at the root): {', '.join(manifests) or 'none found'}. "
                "Strip nested PWA manifests in packaging; a legit nested "
                "manifest needs an explicit ALLOW_NESTED_MANIFESTS entry.",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- duplicate entry names (appending zip tooling) --------------
        dupes = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        if dupes:
            error(
                "duplicate-entries",
                f"{zip_path}: duplicate entry names: {', '.join(dupes)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- junk entries -----------------------------------------------
        junk = sorted(
            n for n in names if os.path.basename(n) == ".DS_Store" or n.startswith("__MACOSX/")
        )
        if junk:
            error(
                "zip-junk",
                f"{zip_path}: store-hostile junk entries: {', '.join(junk)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- empty directories ------------------------------------------
        empty_dirs = sorted(
            n
            for n in names
            if n.endswith("/") and not any(o.startswith(n) and o != n for o in names)
        )
        if empty_dirs:
            error(
                "empty-dirs",
                f"{zip_path}: empty directory entries: {', '.join(empty_dirs)}",
            )
            failures += 1

        # --- root manifest shape: MV3 parse + icons exist ---------------
        if "manifest.json" in names:
            raw = z.read("manifest.json").decode("utf-8")
            # STRICT parse, no comment stripping: the Chrome Web Store
            # uploader rejects // comments ("manifest.json:17:2: missing
            # value", owner report 2026-10-11) even though Chrome's local
            # loader tolerates them. The build script ships a stripped
            # manifest in the zip; the // commenting stays allowed only in
            # the SOURCE file. A zip whose manifest needs stripping to
            # parse is exactly the failure this guard exists to kill.
            try:
                manifest = json.loads(raw)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                error(
                    "manifest-parse",
                    f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json is not STRICT JSON "
                    f"(CWS rejects // comments — the build must package a "
                    f"stripped manifest): {e}",
                )
                failures += 1
                manifest = None
            if isinstance(manifest, dict):
                if "key" in manifest:
                    # CWS upload rule (owner report 2026-10-11: "key field
                    # is not allowed in manifest"): the store owns the
                    # signing key; the source manifest's dev "key" pins the
                    # local id only and must be stripped at packaging.
                    error(
                        "manifest-key",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json carries \"key\" — "
                        "CWS rejects it on upload (the store owns the key; "
                        "the build must strip the dev pin)",
                    )
                    failures += 1
                if manifest.get("manifest_version") != 3:
                    error(
                        "manifest-mv3",
                        f"{zip_path}: root manifest.json manifest_version="
                        f"{manifest.get('manifest_version')!r} — the store "
                        "requires 3",
                    )
…

The README says: "`manifest.json` is plain JSON (Chrome rejects `//` comments; a guard test parses it strictly)". Hmm — one nuance: Chrome's LOCAL loader (unpacked) has historically been tolerant of comments in some versions... but per the CWS report and repo's own guard (ext_package_guard.py comment: "the Chrome Web Store uploader rejects // comments... even though Chrome's local loader tolerates them"), the repo's own docs say Chrome's local loader tolerates them. The ext_package_guard.py says "even though Chrome's local loader tolerates them". And v21_manifest_test.mjs header says "(Chrome's parser is lenient, jsonDecode is not)".

So the PR's README statement "Chrome rejects `//` comments" CONTRADICTS the repo's established understanding ("Chrome's local loader tolerates them; the CWS UPLOADER rejects them"). It's a minor documentation inaccuracy — the true blocker was CWS upload, not local loading. This is a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-level docs nit. The rationale direction is still valid (strict JSON is what the store requires; keeping the source in the same shape the store will consume is defensible and simplifies tooling). Not blocking.

### 3. `test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` (+17, new)

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:test/test.dart';

void main() {
  test(
    'browser_ext/manifest.json is strict JSON (Chrome rejects comments)',
    () {
      final manifest =
          jsonDecode(File('browser_ext/manifest.json').readAsStringSync())
              as Map<String, dynamic>;
      expect(manifest['manifest_version'], 3);
      expect(manifest['permissions'], isA<List>());
    },
  );
}
```

Issues with the test:

**(a) CWD-dependence / path robustness.** `File('browser_ext/manifest.json')` is a relative path. Dart's `dart test` runs with CWD = package root by default, so it works when run from the repo root. BUT: `dart test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` — still package root CWD. OK. However `package_shape_guard_test.dart` has a `_repoRoot()` helper that resolves the repo root robustly, with a comment: "The repo root (dart test runs with the package root as CWD)". The new test uses a bare relative path. This works under `dart test` from repo root but is fragile if the file is ever run via `dart test` from another directory... Actually, `dart test` always sets CWD to the package root regardless of invocation dir? No — `dart test` must be run from the package directory (it resolves the package config). If you run `dart test` in a subdirectory... package:test resolves paths relative to package root. Actually the CWD of the test isolate is the package root. So `File('browser_ext/manifest.json')` resolves against the package root. That's how `chrome_driver.dart`'s `_repoRoot()` works too — it walks up from Directory.current. package_shape_guard_test uses `_repoRoot()` for `Process.runSync` workingDirectory, being defensive.

Hmm, wait — there's a REAL catch: is this repo's `test/` directory part of the ROOT package (`flutter_agent_harness`) or... the root pubspec is at repo root, test/browser_ext is under the root package's test dir. When you run `dart test/browser_ext/manifest_json_test.dart` from repo root, the isolate CWD is repo root. So `browser_ext/manifest.json` resolves fine.

But one edge: `dart test` supports running with `--tags`/presets; the CI runs from repo root. Fine. Still, the more robust pattern in this repo (package_shape_guard_test._repoRoot) exists; the new test's relative path is acceptable since dart test pins CWD. I'd call this a SUGGESTION at most.

**(b) Missing `@TestOn('vm')` annotation.** `dart:io` import means it's VM-only. Other test files in this dir declare `@TestOn('vm')`. Without it, `dart test` default platform is vm anyway. If someone runs the whole suite on the web platform it would fail to compile — but this repo's dart_test.yaml doesn't configure web platforms for the root package. package_shape_guard_test.dart declares `@TestOn('vm')`; the new test doesn't. Minor convention nit (SUGGESTION).

**(c) Tag conventions.** The header comment of package_shape_guard_test says: "no Chrome, no flutter build, so it runs in the default test gate (unlike the rest of test/browser_ext/, which is integration+browser-ext tagged)".
